property_summary: After the admin calls setOwner(0x123) to transfer ownership to 0x123, then a non-admin, non-owner address (0x999) calls setOwner(0x456): in the reference C, the call reverts because onlyAdmin check fails, and owner stays 0x123; in the buggy M, the call also reverts because onlyOwner fails first, but the owner value diverges? Actually both revert. However, the difference is: if admin (who is also owner) calls setOwner(0x456) then owner becomes 0x456 in reference but reverts in buggy M because onlyOwner requires msg.sender == owner (which is true, admin is owner), so both succeed? Wait, the onlyOwner modifier is correct: admin = deployer, owner = deployer initially. So buggy M adds onlyOwner which the deployer already satisfies. Actually the difference is: after setOwner sets owner to a new address, onlyAdmin still refers to original admin, while onlyOwner refers to new owner. That causes divergence. So the concrete scenario: deployer (admin) calls setOwner(0x123) — reference sets owner to 0x123; buggy M reverts because onlyOwner check passes (deployer is owner) and onlyAdmin passes, so it succeeds too. So need a different scenario where onlyOwner fails. For example: let an arbitrary non-admin address (0x111) call setOwner. Reference reverts (onlyAdmin fails). Buggy M also reverts (onlyOwner fails). No divergence. Need scenario where onlyAdmin passes but onlyOwner fails: admin (deployer) first changes owner to another address (0x222) via setOwner (admin call succeeds in reference, but in buggy M this first call fails because onlyOwner? Actually initial owner is deployer, so first setOwner call from deployer passes onlyOwner. So deployer sets owner to 0x222. Then deployer tries to set owner to 0x333: reference succeeds (onlyAdmin passes), buggy M reverts (onlyOwner fails because owner is now 0x222, not deployer). So owner diverges: reference = 0x333, buggy = 0x222. That is the witness scenario.
change_summary: Add onlyOwner modifier instead of onlyAdmin to setOwner function
